title: Franklin that hight Lenehan
html_source: Joyce gets downright Chaucerian again with this phrase. The term “franklin” referred to a wealthy, freeborn non-noble who held property, which seems to allude to the fact that Lenehan folds more bank than his friends (and he’s particularly wealthier than Stephen). “Hight” simply means “named.”
